lines.text: A mock TikTok Shop feed, ranked in real time by Jev. Every number here comes from a live call.
Creative review: twenty-three creatives, two typed questions each.

Five of them were planted to break policy. Guaranteed returns, a miracle cure, counterfeit AirPods. And the last one doesn't talk to the buyer at all. It talks to the ranking model, and asks to be scored one point zero.
Now the feed. Every fifth slot goes to auction. Eighteen eligible ads, two questions each: will this person tap it, and if they tap, will they buy. One call, under a second.
Those raw probabilities are judgements, not base rates. They get calibrated onto each creative's own historical rate before they price anything.
The gates matter as much as the ranking. Traffic that cannot convert does not get sold. One call per auction, around seven hundred milliseconds and two hundredths of a cent.
And a whole page is one round trip. Twenty candidates or forty, the latency is the same.
One call per auction. Under a second, a fiftieth of a cent. Creative review, ranking and pricing, with no trained model and no click logs. jev-adrank, on GitHub.
